A2.txt: Neve Glacier crossing | Glacier travel, short ice steps to ~I2 | Descend ~150-250 ft from the col onto the Neve Glacier and cross roped through its central, less-crevassed section to the ridge near The Horseman on Snowfi

A2.name: Southwest Couloir

A2.name: Standard Route
A2.txt: Gully to saddle | Class 3; ice axe useful early season | Ascend the wide gully/slope to the saddle northwest of the peak.

A2.name: North Face
A2.txt: Avalanche cone and lower face | Neve | The line is the chain of runnels and couloirs just right of the true summit on the north face. Start up the avalanche cone at the foot of the face, then climb neve on the lower face

A2.name: Brothers Traverse (North Peak to South Peak)
A2.txt: Great Basin to the North Brother | Steep snow, then contour | Pass through the notch into the Great Basin, descend steep snow and contour north to the couloir that leads to just below the North Brother's summit. The rout

A2.name: North Peak
A2.txt: Glacier traverse to base | Steep snow, glacier | From Tin Can Gap, drop about 400 ft down steep snow onto the Queest-Alb Glacier. Early season it is a plain snow descent. By late summer expect hard, slippery snow or bare

A2.name: Southeast Ridge
A2.txt: Moat/notch below summit block | Class 3, snow/ice | Cross a moat between rock and ice to gain a notch; hard snow common, ice axe useful.

A2.name: Southeast Gully
A2.txt: Exit to ridge | Steep snow / short mixed | Tops out on the ridge separating the true and false summits. Watch for cornices and for thin snow or a moat where the gully meets the summit rock.

A2.name: Northwest Ridge (Standard Route)
A2.txt: Tailgunner Couloir | Steep snow/grass | Grass and snow patches leading to Tailgunner Pass (roughly 5,320-5,360 ft).

A2.name: Northwest Ridge (Standard Route)
A2.txt: Northwest Ridge | Steep snow, Class 3 | Series of steep snow faces and rock benches; crampons and running belays used on hard/refrozen snow.

A2.name: Northwest Ridge (Standard Route)
A2.txt: Snowfinger (crux) | ~70° snow/ice | Horribly exposed snowfinger below the summit horn; often protected with a picket and belayed or roped.
